# Surgery
## Controls
1. Scan the patient and identify the damaged zone, surface, depth and structure. 2. Use [color=#58e6d9]Open surgical field[/color] on the patient. 3. Select the exact zone on the doll, then select Front, Rear, Left or Right. 4. Set the working depth. The display names the tissue layer under the instrument. 5. Hold an instrument in the active hand and select its mode in the right panel. 6. Draw over the required point with LMB. Use RMB to attach a hemostat or retractor to an incision.
The field refreshes automatically. It shows live physiology, movement, tool sterility, wounds, incision geometry, exposed structures, contamination and attached instruments.
An operating table, authorization, skill, anesthesia and facility are not hard requirements. Surgery can be performed anywhere. Patient movement, unsterile tools and an unprepared field cause displaced contact, contamination, bleeding and infection risk.
An incision is local. Opening one point does not expose the whole body zone. Front, rear, left and right are separate surfaces.
## Instruments
## Opening and closing a site
1. Draw a scalpel stroke over the intended site at the required depth. 2. Control visible bleeding with a hemostat or cautery. 3. Retract the incision. Attach the retractor when continuous exposure is required. 4. Increase depth only after the preceding layer is exposed. 5. Perform the structural operation at the structure shown in the field. 6. Detach instruments from the right panel. 7. Irrigate or debride contaminated tissue. 8. Suture the same incision until it is closed. 9. Repeat the full scan.
## Operations
### External or internal bleeding
1. Select the wound point and depth. 2. Apply Hemostasis or Cautery. 3. For a damaged vessel, expose the vascular layer and apply Vascular repair. 4. Verify both bleed channels, then close.
### Irrigation and debridement
1. Open access to the contaminated depth. 2. Apply Sterile irrigation over the wound. 3. Apply Debridement to infected or necrotic tissue. 4. Irrigate again and close.
### Foreign-body extraction
1. Open access to the depth reported by the scanner. 2. Select Foreign body extraction on the hemostat and apply it to the wound marker. 3. The projectile becomes a physical item in a free hand or beside the patient. 4. Control bleeding, irrigate and close.
### Fracture treatment
1. Expose the structural layer over the confirmed fracture. 2. Apply Bone reduction to remove displacement. 3. Apply Bone fixation to stabilize the bone. 4. Irrigate an open fracture, then close.
### Tendon or nerve repair
1. Expose the displayed tendon or nerve. 2. Apply Tendon repair or Nerve repair directly to the structure. 3. Close the incision.
### Organ repair
1. Open the cavity and retract until the organ is visible. 2. Apply Organ repair inside the organ rectangle. 3. Control cavity bleeding, irrigate and close.
### Cavity drainage
1. Open and retract the thoracic, abdominal, pelvic or cranial cavity. 2. Apply Cavity drainage with the surgical drain to remove an initial volume. 3. Attach the same drain to the incision with RMB for continuous evacuation. 4. Stop the source of internal bleeding before relying on the drain. 5. Detach the drain from the right panel after a full scan confirms that the cavity is clear.
### Cranial and brain surgery
1. Select Head and the correct surface. 2. Incise and retract to the skull. 3. Apply Cranial access to the skull. 4. Advance to the brain and perform repair or extraction. 5. Control bleeding and close.
### Eye repair or removal
1. Select Eyes, expose the eye structure and apply Ophthalmic repair. 2. For removal, apply Organ separation to the exposed eye. 3. Control bleeding and close.
### Organ removal
1. Expose the organ and control its bleeding. 2. Apply Organ separation with the saw directly to the organ. 3. The organ becomes a physical entity. 4. Repair vessels and close.
### Limb amputation
1. Select the exact arm, hand, leg or foot. 2. Incise, retract and control bleeding at the separation line. 3. Apply Controlled amputation with the saw. 4. Repair vessels and close the stump.
### Transplantation or limb reattachment
1. Select the missing zone. 2. Hold the compatible detached part or prosthesis and click it on the patient. The popup confirms staging. 3. Prepare the receiving site. 4. Apply Transplant anastomosis with the suture. 5. Repair vessels and nerves, then close.
### Cyberware installation and service
1. Select the host zone. 2. Hold the physical implant and click it on the patient to stage it. 3. Expose the compatible host structure. 4. Apply Cyberware with the multitool. Installation uses a real compatible slot and calibrates the interface. 5. With no implant staged, applying the same mode directly to an exposed installed module removes that physical module. 6. Repair, cooling and power service use the module's physical service consumables rather than the surgical installation mode. 7. Close and verify the Cyberware scanner tab.
### Regional autopsy
1. The patient must be dead. 2. Select the region and surface. 3. Use Forensic dissection to expose the required structures. 4. Record the findings and suture the incision.
## Persistence
Wounds, missing anatomy, cyberware, cavity blood, incision geometry, depth, contamination and closure survive a round transition. Runtime sessions and attached physical instruments do not.
